main_body: Wide industrial hall: a large corrugated-metal sloped roof with a skylight strip and a brick chimney, over a brick front wall with arched windows, two copper pipes and a riveted double door
top_band: At a middle column: dark ridge at rows ~28-30, a light grey-blue ridge band at ~30-34, a skylight slat strip at ~32-54, then the corrugated roof slope in mid and dark grey-blue to ~90, ending in an orange eave trim line at ~90-93
evidence: The roof is a large sloped surface seen from above, in the same way as the reference house roofs. It is clearly separated from the brick front wall by an orange trim line and a stone cornice with a darker band under it. The front wall is a distinct vertical face. Its arched windows and the door are inset with frames and dark inner edges. There is no receding side face. The roof slope and front wall read as proper 3/4.

style.evidence: The roof has about 4-5 grey-blue steps, vertical corrugation stripes, rust dots and a skylight with glass glints. The brick wall has several brown tones with mortar variation. The windows are lit with glow dots, and the copper pipes and riveted door are detailed. Outlines are tinted dark blue-grey or brown rather than black. The large roof area is somewhat uniform stripes, so it is a little less rich than the Beodeul tile roofs, but there are no large flat fills and it would sit acceptably next to the references.
